2.  The appellants have been convicted and sentenced in connection with SC/ST Case No.07 of 2022 for the offences under Sections 376D, 323, 342, 363 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3(1)(w)(ii) of SC/ST Act.
They have been sentenced to undergo life imprisonment along with fine of Rs.20,000/- for the offence under Section 376 D of the I.P.C. amongst other sentences.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and learned APP for the State and have gone through the impugned judgment, the evidence and the Trial Court Records.

sentences.text: 4 . Opportunity was given to the State to oppose the bail, which the State availed and opposed.
5. We have gone through the evidence of the victim and the deposition of the doctor and also the SFSL report.
From these three evidence, it is clear that rape has been committed upon the victim by these two appellants which is supported by the medical evidence and the SFSL report.
6. Considering the aforesaid fact, we are not inclined to release the appellants on bail.
7. Accordingly, these interlocutory applications stand dismissed.

(ANANDA SEN, J.) (SUBHASH CHAND, J.) R.P.
